overview: This Senate resolution supports National Fentanyl Awareness Day and designates April 29, 2026, as that day. It focuses on fake or counterfeit pills made to look like real prescription drugs but containing fentanyl, a powerful synthetic opioid that can be deadly in very small amounts. Its findings cite Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) data on pill seizures and overdose deaths and point to low awareness among teens and young adults, who can buy such pills through social media. The resolution praises law enforcement efforts against counterfeit pills and encourages using existing legal authority to stop their spread. It is ceremonial and does not create new laws or funding. The Senate agreed to it by unanimous consent on April 29, 2026.
for: Supporters say many young people do not know counterfeit pills may contain fentanyl, and a national awareness day can help prevent overdose deaths.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law or spending, and that awareness alone does not address treatment or prevention resources.
